questions.question: Which of the following liquids can dissolve noble metals such as gold and platinum?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** **____**Aqua regia**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Aqua regia, also known as **king's water**, is a** mixture of nitric acid and hydrochloric acid** in the ratio 1:3 and is used to dissolve noble metals such as gold and platinum.
 
• Only the combination of two acids is capable to dissolve various elements, while individually both HCl and HNO3 are not capable to dissolve them.
 
• It is a **yellow-orange fuming liquid** used to remove metals like gold and platinum from substances, especially in **microelectronics and micro-fabrication labs**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **Formic Acid:**

 
• The simplest form of carboxylic acid, formic acid is present in the venom of red ants. 
 
• Due to its stinging nature, it is used by the ants to kill prey or to protect their nests from predators.
 
• In the case of humans, it is mainly used as a preservative due to its anti-bacterial nature. It is also used in the production of leather, rubber, and cleaning products.

**Acetic Acid:**

 
• Acetic acid is the common name of **ethanoic acid.**
 
• The chemical Formulae for Acetic acid is **CH3COOH.**
 
• It belongs to a group called carboxylic acid and hence they are **weak acids**.
 
• When acetic acid is diluted in water with a percentage of 5-8, then **vinegar** is formed.
 
• The melting point of acetic acid is 290K and it often freezes at room temperature, hence it has another name called **Glacial Acetic Acid.**

**Chloroform:**

 
• Chloroform, or trichloromethane, is an organic compound with the formula **CHCl₃**.
 
• It is a **colorless, volatile, liquid** derivative of trichloromethane with an ether-like odor.
 
• Formerly used as an inhaled** anaesthetic** during the surgery, the primary use of chloroform today is as a **solvent** and in the production of the** refrigerant freon.**

questions.question: The process of ______ is used to increase shelf life of milk by destroying disease causing microorganisms.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**pasteurization.**__

__
 
• **Pasteurization** is the process used to increase the shelf life of milk by destroying disease-causing microorganisms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Pasteurization was invented by French scientist **Louis Pasteur.**
 
• Pasteur discovered that heating milk to a high temperature and then quickly cooling it before bottling or packaging it could keep it fresh for longer.
 
• 
 
The process of pasteurization involves heating milk to **71.7°C for at least 15 seconds and no more than 25 seconds.** Because of the nature of the heat treatment, it sometimes referred to as the** ‘High-Temperature Short Time’ (HTST) process. **

 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Evaporation**__ is the process of conversion of liquid into vapour at any temperature below its boiling point.

 __
 
• It increases with an **increase in surface area and temperature.**
 
• Evaporation of acetone is **used for removing nail polish.**
 
 
 
• **Condensation**__ is the process of conversion of gas into the liquid.
 __
 
• It is the **reverse process of evaporation.**
 
• Solids, liquids, and gases are** interconvertible by changing the condition pressure, and temperature.**
 
 
 
• **Rain falling down** is an example.
 
• **Hydrogenation**__ is the process of treating or combining chemically unsaturated compounds with hydrogen in the presence of a catalyst.
 
 
• Hydrogenation is mainly used in the **food industry, petrochemical industry, and pharmaceutical industry.**
 
• The most common catalysts used for hydrogenation is **Nickel, Platinum, and Palladium.**

questions.question: Galvanisation is a method of protecting steel and iron from rusting by coating them with a thin layer of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zinc**__.

__
 
• **Galvanisation is a method of protecting steel and iron from rusting by coating them with a thin layer of Zinc**.
 
• The galvanizing process consists of three steps
 
 
• Surface preparation
 
• Fuxing
 
• Galvanizing
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Galvanization**

 
 
• Galvanization is the process of **applying a protective layer of zinc to a metal**.
 
• It is a very common method of **preventing the rusting of iron**.
 
• This can be done by dipping the metal to be protected in hot, molten zinc or by the process of electroplating.
 
• The protection of iron and steel from corrosion by coating with molten zinc. 
 
• The **zinc coating protects from the atmosphere the part’s surface,** avoiding corrosion and weathering.
 
• Material is loaded onto jigs before being immersed in molten zinc at about 450 degrees until the working temperature is the same as zinc.
 
• During this process, the molten zinc reacts to a series of zinc/iron alloys with the steel surface.
 
• Galvanization helps extend the life of steel parts by forming a membrane between the metal and the air, preventing the accumulation of iron oxide on the steel layer.
 
• Galvanization also offers superior corrosion resistance to environmentally exposed parts.

questions.question: Whitewashed walls appear to be shiny after three to four days due to the formation of:

• The whitewash contains calcium hydroxide. It forms a thin layer of calcium carbonate on the walls by slowly reacting with carbon dioxide in the air.
 
• After three to four days of whitewashing, calcium carbonate is created.
 
• As a result, after three to four days, the walls have a shiny white finish.
 
• **Ca(OH)₂₍ₐq₎ + CO₂₍g₎ → CaCO₃₍ₛ₎ + H₂O₍ₗ₎**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The chemical compound** calcium carbonate has the formula CaCO₃.** It is the major component of eggshells, gastropod shells, shellfish skeletons, and pearls and is found in rocks such as the minerals calcite and aragonite.
 
• **Calcium nitrate,** is an inorganic chemical with the formula Ca(NO₃)₂ₓ.
 
• **Calcium sulphate** and its hydrates are inorganic compounds with the formula CaSO₄.
 
• **Calcium oxide**, often known as lime or more particularly quicklime, is a white or greyish white solid made by burning calcium carbonate to remove carbon dioxide.

questions.question: Why is water fluoridation, which is the controlled adjustment of fluoride to public water supply, done?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To prevent tooth decay**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Water fluoridation **is the addition of fluoride to a public water supply with** the express purpose of preventing tooth deca**y.
 
• **Fluoridated water **contains a sufficient amount of fluoride to prevent cavities; this can occur naturally or through the addition of fluoride.
 
• Fluoridated water works on dental surfaces by producing low levels of fluoride in saliva, which slows the demineralization of tooth enamel and speeds up the remineralization of tooth enamel in the early stages of cavities.
 
• In most industrialised countries, tooth decay is still a serious public health concern, impacting** 60–90 percent of kids and the vast majority of adults**.
 
• Fluoridation of drinking water decreases cavities in children, but its effectiveness in adults is unclear.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Damage to a tooth's surface,** or enamel, is known as **tooth decay.**
 
• It occurs when oral bacteria produce acids that destroy the enamel.
 
• Cavities (dental caries) are holes in your teeth caused by tooth decay.
 
• If left untreated, dental decay can lead to discomfort, infection, and even tooth loss.
